sentences.text: Hoplosuchus possessed relatively long limbs, a feature indicating it was a terrestrial animal.
The known specimen was approximately 20 cm long, though it might have been a juvenile.
Hoplosuchus is known from a single skeleton found in the Morrison Formation of Utah during road construction.
Charles W. Gilmore named the genus Hoplosuchus in 1926, with H. kayi as the type species.
Due to its small size, Hoplosuchus likely ate insects and small vertebrates, possibly being carnivorous or omnivorous.
A 2017 cladistic analysis recovered Hoplosuchus as a member of the family Protosuchidae.
Hoplosuchus lived during the Tithonian stage, between 149.2 and 145.06 million years ago.
